title: Your AI Assistant Can Now Be Your Ad Studio
paragraphs: Most marketers already use an AI assistant for brainstorming, drafting, and editing. Yet when it is time to turn an idea into an actual ad, they leave the conversation, open another tool, and start over. That context switch is where momentum dies. A newer approach keeps everything in one place by connecting creative tools directly to the assistant you already use. This article explains how that works and how to build a smoother ad workflow around it.
The Problem With Tool-Hopping

A typical ad workflow looks like this: brainstorm angles in a chat, copy the best one, open a design platform, rebuild the brief, generate visuals, export files, and upload them to an ad manager. Every step loses a little context. The assistant that helped you shape the idea cannot see the creative, and the design tool cannot see your reasoning.

The result is slower production and weaker consistency. Details such as tone, audience, and offer get re-explained again and again. Small teams feel this most, because every minute spent moving files is a minute not spent on strategy.
What MCP Changes

MCP, short for Model Context Protocol, is a standard that lets AI assistants connect to outside tools. Instead of you carrying information between apps, the assistant calls the tool directly. You stay in the conversation, describe what you need, and the creative comes back inside the same thread.

For advertisers, this means the brief, the iteration, and the output live together. If the first draft misses the mark, you say so in plain language and the assistant adjusts. There is no re-uploading, no re-briefing, and no hunting for the latest file version.
Making Ads Inside a Conversation

Teams that want to make ads in Claude can describe a product, an offer, and an audience, then ask for image and video concepts without leaving the chat. Predis.ai provides the creative engine behind this setup, so the assistant handles the thinking while the platform handles production.

A good request resembles a short creative brief. State what you sell, who it is for, what action you want, and the tone you prefer. Ask for a few variations rather than one, since comparing options is the fastest way to find a direction worth refining.
Writing Better Briefs for Better Output

The quality of generated ads tracks the quality of your instructions. Vague requests produce generic work. Specific requests produce usable work. Compare “an ad for my shoe brand” with “a square feed ad for lightweight running shoes, aimed at beginners training for a first 10K, friendly tone, with a clear offer for free shipping.”

Include constraints too. Mention platform, format, and anything that must appear, such as a discount or a logo. Mention what to avoid, such as jargon or overly salesy language. Constraints help the assistant stay on target and cut revision rounds.
Iterating Like a Conversation

Because the workflow is conversational, revision becomes natural. Ask for a shorter headline, a warmer tone, a different color mood, or a version aimed at a different audience. Treat each response as a draft and steer it. Predis.ai keeps the output tied to your brand settings, so even fast iterations stay recognizable.
This style of work also encourages testing. When variations cost minutes, you can try several hooks, formats, and offers instead of betting everything on a single concept.
Where Human Judgment Still Matters

Automation speeds up production, but it does not replace judgment. Review every ad for accuracy, claims, and tone before it goes live. Check that prices, dates, and promises are correct. Confirm that the creative matches platform rules and your brand standards.

Strategy remains your job as well. Deciding which audience to target, which offer to lead with, and how much to spend are decisions no assistant should make alone. Use the time you save on production to think harder about those choices.
A Simple Starting Plan

Begin small. Pick one product and one platform. Ask for three distinct angles, choose the strongest, and request two refinements. Publish, measure results for a week, and note what worked. Then repeat with a second product. Within a month you will have a repeatable process and a library of tested ideas.
Final Thoughts

The best tools are the ones that fit the way you already work. Keeping creative production inside your assistant removes friction, preserves context, and shortens the distance between idea and published ad. With a clear brief, a habit of testing, and careful review, small teams can compete with much larger ones. The technology is ready; the advantage goes to those who build a good process around it.

title: Longer AI Video Is Here: What Marketers Can Do With It
paragraphs: Early AI video clips were short, often just a few seconds. That was fine for novelty, but it limited real marketing use. A product story, a tutorial, or a testimonial needs room to breathe. As newer models stretch clip length and improve consistency, the creative possibilities widen. This article explores what longer AI video means for marketers and how to plan content that takes advantage of it.
Why Clip Length Matters

A few seconds is enough for a hook but rarely enough for a message. Longer clips allow a beginning, middle, and end. You can introduce a problem, show a solution, and close with a call to action without stitching several fragments together.

Stitching has its own cost. Each separate clip may differ slightly in lighting, character appearance, or style, and those differences make the final piece feel patchy. A single longer generation tends to feel more cohesive.
Meet a New Option

Marketers looking at a 30-second AI video generator now have models such as Seedance 2.5 to evaluate. It is designed for longer, continuous clips and supports guiding the output with reference images, which helps keep subjects and styles aligned with your brand. Predis.ai lists the model alongside other options, so you can compare it with alternatives in one place.
As with any model, treat claims as a starting point. Test it on your own prompts and judge whether the results fit your needs.
Planning for a Longer Format

A thirty-second video needs structure. Without it, the clip can wander. Try this outline: a three-second hook, a short setup of the problem, a clear demonstration of the benefit, and a closing line with an action. Write this plan before you write the prompt.
Then describe each beat in your prompt. Specify the subject, the setting, the movement, and the mood. The more clearly you describe the sequence, the more likely the model is to deliver it.
Using Reference Images

Reference images are a powerful way to maintain consistency. Provide a product photo, a brand color palette, or an example of the visual style you want. The model uses these as anchors, which reduces surprises and keeps the result closer to your identity.

Choose clear, well-lit references. Avoid cluttered backgrounds, which can confuse the output. If you have several references, make sure they agree with each other in style, since conflicting inputs lead to muddled results.
Where Longer Video Fits

Long clips suit product explainers, quick tutorials, founder messages, and story-driven ads. They also work well for platform formats that reward watch time. A thirty-second piece can be cut into shorter teasers, giving you several assets from one generation.
Predis.ai helps by connecting generation with scheduling, so a clip can move from draft to published post without extra exporting. That saves time when you produce content every week.
Quality Control

Always watch the full clip, not just the opening. Longer generations give more room for drift, such as faces subtly changing or objects shifting. Check audio or captions if they are present, and verify that nothing misleading appears on screen.
Generate more than one version. Compare them, choose the strongest, and consider regenerating once more with a refined prompt. Iteration is a normal part of the process.
Budgeting Time and Cost

Longer clips usually cost more to generate than short ones. Use shorter drafts to test ideas, then spend on a longer version only when a concept has proven itself. This approach keeps experimentation affordable while protecting the quality of your flagship content. Predis.ai makes it easy to move between options as your needs change.
Final Thoughts

Longer AI video expands what small teams can produce, turning rough ideas into complete stories. Plan your structure, use reference images, review carefully, and iterate. The tools will keep improving, but the fundamentals remain the same: a clear message, a defined audience, and content worth watching from the first second to the last.

title: Learn From the Market: A Smarter Way to Research Competitor Advertising
paragraphs: Every advertiser has wondered what competitors are running, which messages they keep repeating, and which offers they quietly drop. The answers are valuable, because ads that stay live for a long time usually signal something is working. Researching this by hand, however, is tedious and inconsistent. This article explains how to approach competitor ad research systematically and turn what you learn into better creative.
Why Competitor Ads Are a Goldmine

Advertising is public by nature. Brands pay to put messages in front of audiences, which means those messages can be studied. Looking at them reveals positioning, pricing angles, creative formats, and seasonal strategies. It also shows gaps, such as audiences or pain points nobody seems to address.
The goal is not imitation. Copying a rival erases what makes you distinct. The goal is understanding the landscape so you can choose where to compete and where to differentiate.
What to Look For

Start with longevity. An ad that runs for months has likely earned its budget, while one that disappears after days probably underperformed. Next, study hooks, the first line or visual that grabs attention. Note whether competitors lead with a question, a result, a testimonial, or a discount.

Then examine formats. Are rivals favoring short video, static images, or carousels? Look at calls to action and landing page promises. Finally, watch frequency of change. A brand refreshing creative weekly is testing aggressively, and that tells you something about its priorities.
The Manual Approach and Its Limits

Many teams browse public ad libraries and take screenshots. This works at first, but it breaks down quickly. Screenshots pile up without structure, comparisons are subjective, and it is easy to miss changes over time. A one-time review also goes stale within weeks.
Research needs to be ongoing to be useful. Markets shift, offers rotate, and new entrants appear. Ongoing monitoring catches those changes while they still matter.
Using Tools to Stay Current

Dedicated tools make the process repeatable. When you track competitor ads with a purpose-built system, you can follow multiple brands in one place and see how their creative evolves. Predis.ai offers this through its Ad Intelligence feature, which is designed to help marketers research Meta advertising without building spreadsheets by hand.
The benefit is consistency. Instead of occasional manual checks, you get a steady view of what the market is doing, which makes patterns far easier to spot.
Turning Research Into Action

Insight only matters if it changes what you make. After each review, write down three takeaways. Perhaps competitors all lean on discounts, which suggests an opening for a quality-focused message. Perhaps nobody uses customer stories, which suggests an underused angle.

Then translate those takeaways into test ideas. Create a few ad variations that explore the gap, run them against your current best performer, and measure the difference. Predis.ai can help you generate those variations quickly, so research flows directly into production.
Building a Research Routine

Set a weekly or biweekly slot for review. Keep it short, around thirty minutes. Check the brands you follow, note new creative, and flag anything unusual. Maintain a simple log with dates, observations, and ideas to test. Over a few months this log becomes a valuable record of how your market moves.
Limit your list. Following five to ten relevant competitors beats skimming fifty. Include a mix of direct rivals and adjacent brands that reach the same audience.
Ethics and Judgment

Competitor research should stay within public information. Study publicly visible ads, respect intellectual property, and never reproduce another brand’s creative. Use what you learn as input for original work. Strong brands win by saying something distinct, not by echoing everyone else.
Final Thoughts

Understanding competitor advertising reduces guesswork. It tells you what the market rewards, where it is crowded, and where room remains. Combine regular monitoring with disciplined testing and your creative decisions become grounded in evidence rather than hunches. Start with a short list, review on a schedule, and let each insight shape your next experiment.

title: Keep the Conversation Going: Image Generation Without Leaving Your Chat
paragraphs: Designing a visual often starts with a conversation: what should it show, who is it for, what mood fits? Then comes the awkward part, where you leave the discussion, open a separate tool, and try to recreate the idea from memory. A growing set of integrations removes that gap by letting your assistant create images directly. This article explains the approach and how to use it well.
Why Separate Tools Slow You Down

Every tool switch costs context. You explain your idea to the assistant, then explain it again to the image tool. If the result misses, you return to the chat, describe the problem, copy the revised prompt, and try again. That loop is slow and error-prone.
For teams producing visuals regularly, the lost time compounds. Social graphics, ad creatives, thumbnails, and blog headers all follow the same pattern, and each round trip chips away at your day.
A Connected Approach

Integrations built on MCP, a standard for connecting assistants to outside tools, let the assistant request images itself. You describe the visual in conversation, and the result appears in the same thread. Revisions happen the same way, through plain-language feedback.

If you want to generate images in Claude, Predis.ai offers an image generation MCP that connects its creative engine to your assistant. That keeps ideation and production in one place and shortens the path from concept to finished graphic.
Writing Prompts That Produce Usable Images

Good image prompts are specific. Describe the subject, the setting, the style, the lighting, and the composition. State the intended use, such as a square social post or a wide blog header, so the framing suits the format.

Avoid vague phrases like “nice” or “professional.” Replace them with concrete descriptions, such as “clean white background, soft shadows, centered product, minimal styling.” Concrete language gives the model something to work with.
Iterating Efficiently

Treat the first result as a draft. Ask for specific changes: a warmer palette, a closer crop, a simpler background, or more space for text. Change one thing at a time so you can see what each instruction does.

Generating several variations early helps too. Comparing options side by side makes preferences clear faster than debating a single image. Predis.ai supports this kind of rapid exploration, so you can settle on a direction quickly.
Matching Images to Purpose

Different tasks call for different visuals. Ads need strong focal points and room for copy. Blog headers benefit from simple, atmospheric compositions. Product visuals demand accuracy and clean lighting. Social posts often reward bold color and clear subjects.
Decide the purpose before you generate. Knowing the end use helps you describe the right format, aspect ratio, and mood, and it prevents wasted attempts.
Protecting Brand Consistency

Generated images can drift from your identity without guidance. Share your brand colors, style notes, and any visual rules at the start of the session. Reuse the same descriptors across prompts so results feel related.
Review outputs against your brand standards before publishing. A small mismatch in tone or color may not seem important, but repeated across a feed it weakens recognition.
Review and Responsibility

Always inspect generated images closely. Check for distorted details, unreadable text, and anything that could mislead viewers. Avoid imitating real individuals without permission, and respect copyright and platform rules.
Where appropriate, disclose that visuals are AI-generated. Transparency builds trust with audiences who increasingly care about authenticity.
Final Thoughts

Image creation works best when it stays close to your thinking. By generating visuals in the same conversation where ideas form, you reduce friction, preserve context, and move faster. Write specific prompts, iterate in small steps, and keep your brand in view. The result is a smoother workflow and better visuals with less effort.

title: Telling a Story in Scenes: Why Multi-Shot AI Video Matters
paragraphs: Professional video rarely consists of one continuous shot. Wide shots establish the setting, close-ups show emotion, and cuts maintain energy. Early AI tools struggled here because each clip stood alone. Newer models aim to handle sequences, keeping characters and settings steady across shots. This article explains why that matters and how to use it to make more convincing marketing videos.
The Consistency Challenge

Anyone who has generated several AI clips knows the frustration. The character in the second clip looks different from the first. The outfit changes. The room shifts. These mismatches break the illusion and make a video feel amateur.
For marketing, consistency matters even more. A brand mascot, a spokesperson, or a recurring product must look the same across scenes. Otherwise, viewers notice, and trust drops.
What Multi-Shot Means

Multi-shot generation lets you describe a sequence of scenes in one request. The model plans transitions and tries to keep subjects stable. Instead of generating five clips and hoping they match, you guide the story from start to finish.

If you are exploring a multi-shot AI video generator, Kling 3.0 Pro is one model to evaluate, especially for character consistency across scenes. Predis.ai includes it among its available models, so you can compare it with others using the same prompts.
Structuring a Multi-Shot Prompt

Think like a director. Break your idea into shots and describe each briefly. For example: a wide shot of a busy kitchen, a close-up of hands preparing the product, a medium shot of the customer smiling, and a final shot of the product with the logo.

Keep descriptions of the main character identical across shots. Repeat key details such as clothing, hair, and setting so the model has consistent anchors. Specify camera moves sparingly, since too many instructions can compete with each other.
Ideal Use Cases

Multi-shot video suits testimonials, product stories, how-to sequences, and brand films. It also helps with ads that need a quick narrative arc: problem, solution, result. These formats benefit from cuts that keep viewers engaged.
Short social ads can use two or three shots to feel dynamic without becoming confusing. Longer pieces can use more, as long as the story stays clear.
Keeping Your Brand Intact

Fast generation can drift from your identity if you are not careful. Define colors, tone, and visual style before you start. Use reference material where available. Predis.ai lets you maintain brand settings so the content still feels like it belongs to your company, even when you are experimenting with different models.
Testing Across Models

No single model wins at everything. Run the same multi-shot prompt through two or three options and compare results. Look at character stability, transitions, motion quality, and how closely the output follows your instructions. Note which model handles people best and which handles products best.
Keep a simple record of your tests. Over time, you will know which tool to reach for depending on the task, which speeds up future work.
Review Before Publishing

Check every shot. Look for odd hands, shifting backgrounds, and mismatched details between scenes. Confirm that any text on screen is accurate. If a shot is weak, regenerate that section rather than discarding the whole project.
Also consider disclosure. Follow the rules of the platforms you publish on and be transparent where required. Trust is easy to lose and hard to rebuild.
Final Thoughts

Multi-shot generation moves AI video closer to real storytelling. With careful planning, consistent descriptions, and honest testing, marketers can produce sequences that feel intentional rather than random. Start with a three-shot idea, learn from the result, and expand from there. Good stories still begin with a clear message; the tools simply make telling them faster.

title: From Product Page to Promo: Faster Video Ads for Online Stores
anchor: product video from a product link
paragraphs: Running an online store means constantly feeding the marketing machine. New products, seasonal sales, and restocks all need visuals. Producing a video for every item is a heavy lift, especially when the catalog is large. Fortunately, AI tools are making it possible to start from the information you already have: your product pages. This article explains how to turn listings into effective ads.
The Catalog Problem

A store with fifty products needs fifty sets of creative, and every price change or new variant creates more work. Teams often focus on bestsellers and leave the rest without good visuals, which quietly limits sales.

The raw material already exists. Product pages contain titles, descriptions, images, prices, and reviews. The challenge is turning that information into engaging ads without starting from scratch each time.
Starting From Links and Data

Modern tools can ingest this information directly. Instead of rewriting a brief for every item, you provide the link and let the tool gather details. If you want a product video from a product link, Predis.ai’s ecommerce MCP connects its creative engine to your AI assistant for that purpose. It is also designed for bulk workflows such as generating ads from a CSV of products.
This approach saves time on every item, and it keeps messaging consistent with what customers see on the page.
Preparing Your Product Pages

Output quality depends on input quality. Make sure product images are clear and well lit. Write descriptions that state concrete benefits rather than generic praise. Keep prices and availability accurate.
Strong source material gives the tool more to work with and reduces the need for manual fixes. Think of your product page as the creative brief.
Choosing the Right Ad Style

Different products suit different approaches. Visual items such as fashion or decor often work well with lifestyle scenes. Practical products benefit from demonstrations that show how they work. Gifts and seasonal items can lean on emotion and timing.

User-generated style ads, with casual and personal tone, can build trust because they feel closer to a recommendation than a commercial. Predis.ai supports several styles, so you can match the format to the product and platform.
Working in Bulk

When you have many products, structure matters. Organize your data in a spreadsheet with clear columns for product name, link, key benefit, and target audience. Start with a small batch of five to ten items to check the output quality before scaling up.
Review samples before generating the full set. Fixing a problem in the template is much cheaper than fixing it across hundreds of ads.
Testing What Sells

Create at least two variations for your most important products. Test different hooks, such as a price-focused opening versus a benefit-focused one. Track click-through rate, cost per purchase, and return on ad spend.
Retire weak ads quickly and invest more in winners. Because production is faster, you can refresh creative regularly and avoid fatigue.
Staying Accurate and Compliant

Ecommerce ads carry real commitments. Verify every price, discount, shipping claim, and product feature before publishing. Make sure ads match what the landing page says, since mismatches frustrate customers and may violate platform policies.
Review all outputs for visual accuracy too. Confirm that colors, sizes, and details represent the real product. Misleading visuals lead to returns and lost trust.
Keeping Brand Identity

Even at scale, your ads should feel like they belong to one store. Set your logo, colors, fonts, and tone once and apply them across every creative. Predis.ai keeps these settings available so large batches still look cohesive.
Final Thoughts

Ecommerce marketing rewards speed and consistency, and both improve when creative production starts from the data you already have. Prepare good product pages, test in small batches, review carefully, and scale what works. With a clear process, even a small team can keep every product visible without burning out.

title: Video Production Inside a Chat: A New Workflow for Busy Marketers
paragraphs: Video takes longer than almost any other content format. Scripting, generating, reviewing, and exporting each involve a different tool or person. For small teams, that complexity often means video gets postponed. A newer workflow brings video generation into the assistant you already talk to, shrinking the steps between an idea and a finished clip.
Why Video Feels So Hard

The main obstacle is not creativity but logistics. You need a script, visuals, motion, sometimes voice, captions, and the right format for each platform. Coordinating all of that across separate apps eats hours.
Even with AI generators, the process often involves copying prompts between windows, downloading files, and re-uploading them elsewhere. Those handoffs introduce delays and mistakes.
Video Inside the Assistant

MCP is a standard that lets AI assistants connect with outside tools. With a video integration, you describe what you want in conversation and the assistant requests the clip directly. Feedback happens in the same thread, so revisions feel like ordinary dialogue.

Teams wanting to make videos in Claude can use Predis.ai’s AI video MCP, which connects the platform’s generation capabilities to the assistant. You get scripting help and production in one place, which keeps the whole project coherent.
Starting With a Strong Brief

Treat every request like a creative brief. Say what the video is for, who will watch it, how long it should be, and what action viewers should take. Describe the tone and visual style. Mention platform, since vertical clips for stories differ from wide clips for websites.
A useful structure is hook, value, and call to action. Ask the assistant to draft this outline first, approve it, and only then generate the video. Planning before generating saves credits and time.
Iterating Through Conversation
After the first clip appears, give targeted feedback. Ask for a faster pace, a different opening, a calmer mood, or a shorter runtime. Be specific about what to change and what to keep.
Generate a few variations of the hook, since the opening seconds decide whether people keep watching. Predis.ai makes producing alternatives quick, so testing becomes realistic even for small teams.
Choosing the Right Format
Short vertical clips suit social discovery. Square clips fit feeds. Wider clips suit websites and presentations. Decide the format before generating so the framing works from the start.
Captions deserve attention, because many viewers watch without sound. Make sure text is readable, timed well, and placed where it will not be covered by platform interface elements.
Building a Repeatable Routine

Set a weekly session. Spend the first part brainstorming topics with your assistant, the second generating and refining clips, and the last scheduling them. Keep a running list of ideas so you never start from nothing.
Reuse what works. If a particular hook style or format performs well, create more in that style. Over time, your routine becomes faster and your results more predictable.
Quality and Ethics

Always watch each clip fully before publishing. Look for visual glitches, odd motion, and incorrect text. Verify any claims. Respect platform rules, avoid imitating real people without consent, and follow disclosure guidelines where they apply.
Human oversight is what keeps automated content trustworthy. The assistant speeds up production, but accountability stays with you.
Final Thoughts

Bringing video generation into a conversation removes much of the friction that makes video feel daunting. With clear briefs, thoughtful iteration, and careful review, small teams can publish video regularly without a full production setup. Start with one short clip, learn from the response, and build the habit from there.

title: Taking Visual Content Global: Localizing Images With AI
anchor: translate text in images with Nano Banana Pro
paragraphs: Expanding into new markets usually means translating more than words on a page. Banners, product graphics, social posts, and infographics all carry text baked into the image. Recreating each one for every language has traditionally meant repeated design work. AI image models are starting to make that process far lighter. This article looks at how to localize visuals efficiently.
The Hidden Cost of Localization

Translating a caption is easy. Translating a graphic is not. The new text may be longer or shorter, the layout may break, and fonts may not support certain scripts. A designer often has to rebuild each version by hand.
Multiply that by dozens of assets and several languages, and localization becomes a major project. Many small brands simply skip it, which limits their reach.
What Image Models Can Do

Newer image models can edit existing visuals, including changing text while keeping the rest of the design intact. If you want to translate text in images with Nano Banana Pro, you can start from a finished graphic and ask the model to render the same design in another language. Predis.ai lists the model among its image options, so you can try it alongside alternatives.
Results vary by language and design complexity, so treat the first outputs as drafts to review.
Preparing Source Images

Quality in, quality out. Begin with a clean, high-resolution original. Make sure the text is legible and the layout has some breathing room, since translations often expand. Avoid placing text over busy backgrounds that could confuse the model.
Keep a master version of every asset. That file becomes the reference for every translation, which helps preserve consistent style.
Writing Clear Instructions

Tell the model exactly what to change and what to keep. For example: “Translate all text into Spanish, keep the layout, colors, and product image unchanged.” Provide the exact wording if you have approved translations. Do not rely on the model to choose marketing phrasing, since literal translations can sound awkward.
Where possible, have a native speaker review the copy first. Using vetted text in your prompt produces better and safer results.
Handling Common Challenges

Text length is the most frequent issue. German or Russian can run longer than English, while Chinese or Japanese can run shorter. Allow flexibility in layout. Check line breaks, spacing, and alignment after generation.
Cultural fit matters too. Colors, symbols, and imagery carry different meanings across regions. Review visuals for anything that may confuse or offend local audiences.
Using Multiple References

Some models accept several reference images at once. That helps when you want to keep a product, a logo, and a style consistent in a new version. Provide clear references and describe how each should be used. Predis.ai allows you to combine model options with brand settings, so localized versions still match your identity.
A Practical Workflow

Start with your best-performing asset. Choose one target language, generate a translated version, and have a native speaker review it. Fix errors, publish, and measure results. If performance is strong, expand to additional languages.
Track which regions respond best. Localization takes effort, so prioritize markets that show real interest.
Quality Control and Honesty

Never publish without checking every word. Even small spelling errors can damage credibility. Confirm that prices, dates, and legal text are accurate for each region. Respect local advertising rules and be transparent where AI-generated content must be disclosed.
Final Thoughts

Localization no longer has to mean rebuilding every graphic from scratch. By starting with clean originals, giving precise instructions, and involving native reviewers, brands can reach new audiences faster. Begin with one asset and one language, learn from the process, and scale gradually. Good communication across borders is still about care, and AI simply gives you more time to apply it.
